# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2005 Summary

## Core Principles
The manifesto is built on three guiding values: **Freedom** (individuals governing their own lives), **Fairness** (ensuring everyone has essential requirements for real choices), and **Trust** (giving citizens power to hold government accountable).

## Key Policy Areas

### Healthcare
The party pledges free personal care for elderly and disabled people, funded by a 50% tax rate on incomes over £100,000. They promise quicker diagnosis for serious conditions, free eye and dental checks, reduced prescription charges, and 8,000 more doctors plus 12,000 more nurses. They oppose Labour's targets, preferring clinical decisions made by health professionals.

### Education
The manifesto commits to abolishing all tuition and top-up fees, providing grants for poorer students. They propose cutting infant class sizes to an average of 20 using the £1.5 billion Child Trust Fund. All children would be taught core subjects by qualified specialists, with reformed vocational training alongside academic pathways.

### Economy and Tax
The party commits to economic stability, tough spending choices, and fairer taxation. They propose replacing Council Tax with Local Income Tax, saving typical households £450 annually. Only one net tax rise is proposed: 50% on incomes exceeding £100,000 (affecting 1% of taxpayers). They pledge to abolish the Department of Trade and Industry and cut business red tape.

### Crime and Justice
Plans include 10,000 additional police officers funded by scrapping ID cards, plus 20,000 community support officers. They oppose ID cards as expensive and ineffective, preferring investment in intelligence and investigation. The party supports rehabilitation through community work and prisoner education, while firmly opposing detention without trial.

### Pensions
Pensioners over 75 would receive at least £109.45 weekly (over £100 monthly increase). A "Citizen's Pension" based on residency rather than national insurance contributions would help 2.8 million women currently receiving minimal pensions.

### Environment
Environmental policy runs throughout the manifesto. Key commitments include 20% renewable electricity by 2020, no replacement of nuclear power stations, promoting cycling and walking, tackling waste through 60% recycling targets, and leading international climate negotiations.

### Europe and International Affairs
The party opposed the Iraq war but acknowledges moral obligations toward Iraq's stabilisation. They support EU membership and the proposed constitution (subject to referendum), UN reform, and increasing aid spending to 0.7% of national income by 2011.

### Constitutional Reform
Proposals include curbing Prime Ministerial powers, introducing proportional representation (STV) for elections, a predominantly elected House of Lords, and strengthening local democracy by reducing central government control.

## Funding Approach
All policies are fully costed. Savings come from abolishing the DTI (£8 billion over parliament), scrapping ID cards and the Child Trust Fund. The single tax increase on high earners funds free university education, elderly care, and reduced local taxes.
